newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Platinum and palladium seen lower.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Platinum and palladium seen lower.

text.p: SPOT NY CLOSE * SUPPORT * RESIST * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30

Platinum and palladium prices are likely to trend lower on Wednesday following a statement from Russian state export agency Almazjuvelirexport that it would resume exports at the "nearest" possible time.
Platinum may test support at $450.00 and $440.00, while palladium could head towards $200.00, traders and analysts said.

PLATINUM - Looking to hold support at $450.00 to offset a downside retracement to $440.00 following comments by an agency official of Almazjuvelirexport (Almaz) that Russia would resume exports of platinum group metals (PGMs) at the "nearest" possible time.

Late on Tuesday prices moved to test levels below $450.00 as Russia gave further indications that metal would be shipped soon. But despite Far Eastern selling, platinum was finding robust underlying support in early European trading on Wednesday.
"Prices are likely to calm following the recent volatility," one trader said.

"However, the market will remain tight even if Russian exports resume," the trader said. "There is likely to be still a shortfall in the market, which should underpin a market that is showing signs of turning lower."
Traders suggested that if prices held $450.00, a range roughly between $450 and $470 could be established.
Last week the price of platinum, against the backdrop of an extremely tight physical market, soared to critical resistance at $500. Traders said those levels were unlikely to be visited on Wednesday.

Palladium might test support at $200.00 as speculators and longs liquidated following the recent rise to 17-year highs of around $240.00. A break below $200.00 could spark a retracement to $170.00, traders said.
At 0715 GMT platinum was indicated at $450.00/$455.00, versus Tuesday's London close of $440.10/$445.10. Palladium was at $210.00/$215.00, against $205.60/$210.60.
GOLD - Seen stable with an upside bias. "The market may trend higher after bouncing away from downside support at around $340.00," a trader said.

Resistance around $346.60 continued to keep the market in check, Martin Squires of Rudolf Wolff said, referring to the Comex June contract said. "However, following the impressive bounce towards the tail end of last week we remain moderately bullish and look for further challenges of overhead supply."
Gold at 0715 was quoted at $343.25/$343.75, compared with $343.50/$344.00.
SILVER - Seen consolidating above $470.00 but might try to move towards resistance at $4.90 on strengthening technicals.
A break above $4.90 could prompt a move to $5.00 and possibly $5.20.
Support for silver was pegged at $4.60. It was last at $475/$4.77, a loss of two cents.
